mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand for corporate goods and services, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing wage growth and corporate profit margins, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) and a deceleration in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1 standard deviation from their respective 12-month means indicates a shift from consumer durables to capital goods, which historically precedes cyclical equity drawdowns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > +1σ and HOUST < -1σ in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is above and HOUST is below their respective 12-month mean by one standard deviation in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 3% during a period of negative core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%) signals a policy-driven liquidity expansion that boosts risk asset valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops > 0.75pp in one month AND CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS falls sharply and CPIAUCSL is below 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which historically supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA by >2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained above-trend payroll employment growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous surge in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) by more than 1 standard deviation from their 12-month means indicates a precautionary savings regime, which typically precedes equity market weakness over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > +1σ AND GDPC1 < -1σ in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is above and GDPC1 is below their respective 12-month means by one standard deviation in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 0.5% for five consecutive months signals an expansionary supply cycle that boosts corporate revenues and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA by >0.5% for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained above-trend industrial production growth.
